miles southwest of Prescott, moving northeast at 50 mph.

280.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 21 at 6:55AM EDT until October 22 at 4:00PM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in Charles and King George Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM EDT Thursday, especially around the time of
high tide.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, water reaches yards near Cobb Island
and docks near Dahlgren.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides one and a half to two feet above
normal. The next high tide at Goose Bay is at 1:10 PM and 1:30
AM. The next high tide at Dahlgren is at 11:44 AM and 12:06 AM.
The next high tide at Indian Head is at 5:04 PM and 5:24 AM.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 21 at 4:43AM MDT until October 23 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Scattered thunderstorms across higher terrain Wednesday afternoon
could produce locally heavy rainfall across the eastern San Juan
Mountains and the Upper Rio Grande Valley. Ample sub-tropcial
moisture will then bring periods of moderate to heavy rain across
the area Wednesday night into Thursday morning, which will
continue through the day Friday before winding down Friday
afternoon.
- The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

destination.
